title: The Electric path is asked of the effect's controller, not the Electric source's controller
summary: R4 (and R317) give the choice of the Electric path to the Electric source's controller. The orchestrator's known-divergence list and the pilot verifier record that the engine asks the effect's controller. Every Electric source in the pool today is a spell or a spell effect, so the two players coincide in every test; 05-rulings asserts the source's controller only in that coinciding case. The rule states the ruling. Round-1 verifier measured it: dealEffectDamageAll raises the electricPath decision for ctx.controller, while the Piercing split beside it already uses the source unit's controller (probe 'attr.electric.chooser').

evidence.quote: The **Electric source's controller** chooses the path.

title: Afflicting test title says the OWNER of the killed unit gains the rot; the card says its controller
summary: Umbral Decay prints "those units' controllers gain a rot". The 42-dark-b test is titled "rots the owner of what it kills". In the test the owner and the controller are the same player, so it passes either way, and no test covers a stolen unit killed by an Afflicting source. Retitle the test, and add a case where controller and owner differ.

evidence.quote: Umbral Decay: two -1/-1 counters, and {Afflicting} rots the owner of what it kills

title: Modular would be shared through a column if a unit ever printed it
summary: The owner ruling (Caleb's "Modular is also special", in R294) is that Modular is not a column-shared attribute. R294 itself records that Modular is in the engine's shared attribute set and is harmless only because the one card that prints it is a spell. The round-1 verifier confirmed colAttrs would union it. Latent: no unit prints Modular today; 298 §5c guards the premise, not the non-sharing.

evidence.quote: statement. {Modular} *is* in `attrs`, and is harmless only because the one card

title: Reaping never loses Reaping after drawing (printed second sentence not built)
summary: Reaping's reminder says the source loses Reaping until regroup after drawing. R283 §2 says this is deliberately not built because every Reaping printer is a one-shot spell; the round-1 verifier confirmed nothing removes Reaping after a draw. Latent: becomes live the day a unit can carry Reaping. 263 §4 guards the premise.

title: Piercing excess redirected again by a second Oorblak
summary: replaceCombatDamage offers each holder's leftover to the next replaceCombatDamageToPlayer holder. With two Oorblaks, 10 Piercing combat damage kills both and only 2 reach the player. The designer says 4 go into Oorblak and the other 6 reach the player, because a replacement applies only once. Measured by probe 'attr.piercing.redirect'.
